purpose: Exercise expanding-origin numerical versus event-text prediction on the official TimesX KRW export. Cannot satisfy the primary Seoul protocol because historical publication/snapshot provenance is absent.
dataset: TimesX USDtoKRW, all 66 supplied origins; chosen for Korean currency relevance before measuring model outcomes
target: 100 * (mean of next 12 provided business-day values / last historical value - 1), percentage points
training: Expanding origins, at least 16 earlier samples; only training windows whose final target date is strictly before current origin. Training label release dates remain unverified.
model: Ridge regression with mean squared loss + 1.0 * squared coefficients, unpenalized intercept, train-only feature standardization; identical penalty for all arms, no tuning
features: B1: numeric lag returns at 1/5/12/24/48/95 steps, 12/48-step volatility, calendar sin/cos month, weekday, 9 covariates min/max/mean/median/trend from exported historical summaries, holiday count. B2 adds 32 signed SHA256 hashed English word features with per-document L2 normalization and event count. Strip prediction-window prefix. No pretrained model. B3 adds event count only. B4 adds preceding-origin event text and count only, as a stale-text control.
baseline: B0 flat forecast implies zero mean future change
primary: B1 minus B2 paired MAE; all origins and blocks reported
uncertainty: Moving-block bootstrap, length 3 origins, 5000 draws, seed 20261026; percentile 95% CI. Latest block under 12 origins is automatically too small for confirmatory claims. No current-success probabilities.
gates: No approval regardless of performance: source publication timestamps, original historical snapshots, numerical vintages and exact collection mechanism not verified. Five percent relative improvement is descriptive only. Original protocol.json remains unchanged.
limitations: No probabilistic calibration or business-warning test
Not a reproduction of the published TimesX model
